**Sikhae (시계) – Korean Traditional Rice Cake** Sikhae is a simple, comforting dish made from steamed rice flour (also called “sikhae” or “rice cake”) mixed with water and a pinch of salt. It’s often served as a side dish (banchan) or as a snack. Below is a straightforward recipe you can try at home. --- ### Ingredients | Ingredient | Amount | Notes | |------------|--------|-------| | Rice flour (short‑grain, Korean “sikhae” flour) | 1 cup (≈120 g) | If you can’t find Korean rice flour, use regular short‑grain rice flour. | | Water | 1 ½ cups (≈360 ml) | Adjust slightly for desired consistency. | | Salt | ¼ teaspoon | Optional, for flavor. | | Optional add‑ins | | • Sesame seeds (for garnish)
• Gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes)
• Soy sauce or sesame oil (for dipping) | --- ### Equipment - Mixing bowl - Whisk or spoon - Steamer basket or a pot with a steaming rack - Heat‑resistant plate or tray - Optional: small saucepan for boiling water --- ### Instructions #### 1. Prepare the Steamer 1. Fill a pot with about 2 cm of water. 2. Place a steamer basket or a heat‑resistant plate inside the pot. 3. Bring the water to a gentle boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. #### 2. Mix the Dough 1. In a mixing bowl, combine the rice flour and salt. 2. Gradually pour in the water while whisking continuously to avoid lumps. 3. Stir until you get a smooth, thick batter. - **Tip:** If the batter is too thick, add a little more water (a tablespoon at a time). If it’s too thin, add a pinch more flour. #### 3. Steam the Dough 1. Pour the batter into the steamer basket or onto the plate. 2. Cover the pot with a lid. 3. Steam for **15–20 minutes** or until the dough becomes translucent and firm. - **Check:** Insert a toothpick or a knife; it should come out clean. #### 4. Cool & Slice 1. Remove the steamed dough from the steamer and let it cool for a few minutes. 2. Transfer it to a cutting board. 3. Slice into bite‑size pieces or thin strips, depending on your preference. #### 5. Serve 1. Arrange the sliced sikhae on a plate. 2. Sprinkle with sesame seeds or gochugaru if desired. 3. Serve with a small bowl of soy sauce or sesame oil for dipping. --- ### Variations & Tips | Variation | How to Add | |-----------|------------| | **Savory** | Mix in a tablespoon of finely chopped scallions or minced garlic before steaming. | | **Sweet** | Add a teaspoon of sugar or honey to the batter. | | **Cheese** | Sprinkle grated cheese on top before steaming for a cheesy twist. | | **Texture** | For a chewier texture, use a higher ratio of water (about 1 ¾ cups). | --- ### Storage - Store leftover sikhae in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to **3 days**. - Reheat in a steamer or microwave for a few seconds before serving. Enjoy your homemade sikhae! It’s a quick, versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with kimchi, pickled vegetables, or a light soup.
